title: Existence and Uniqueness of the Viscous Burgers’ Equation Based on Ellis Model
content: In this paper, we investigate the existence and uniqueness of solutions for the viscous Burgers’ equation for the isothermal flow of Ellis fluids  $$\partial_t u + u \partial_x u=\nu\partial_x \left(\phi^{-1}\left (\partial_x u\right)\right)$$  with the initial condition $u(0, x)=u_0$, $0<x<l$, and the boundary condition $u(t, 0)=u(t, l)=0$, $0<t<T$, where $\phi(\tau)=\left[1+c\left|\tau \right|^{\alpha-1}\right] \tau $, $0<c<\infty$, $0<\alpha<\infty$, $\nu$ is the kinematic viscosity, $\tau$ is the shear stress, $u$ is the velocity of the fluid  and $l, T>0$. We proved the existence and uniqueness of solution $u \in L^2\left(0, T; {W_0}^{1,p}(0, l)\right)$  for $u_0\in W^{1,p}_0(0,l)$, where $p=1+ \frac{1}{\alpha}$. Moreover, numerical solutions to the problem are constructed by applying the modeling and simulation package COMSOL® Multiphysics 6.0 to show the images of the solutions.
